*`If you have some understanding of GameMaker Language or programming in general, this page should assist you in making mods for Nuclear Throne Together. It provides answers to the most common questions, documentation on Nuclear Throne’s systems, and documentation on some useful GameMaker systems.`*

`Values`  
`How to find the value of a variable, or any other in-game info.`  
`The function trace(...values) allows you to print value(s) to the chat.`  
`Using this, you can display values like so:`

| trace(Player.maxspeed) trace(instance\_number(enemy)) with(Bandit) trace(my\_health, maxhealth) |
| :---- |

`The command /gml also has a shorthand version: /gml =Player.maxspeed`  
`For Player-specific information, you can also use 0 instead of Player: /gml =0.maxspeed`

# 

# **`[ How To ]`**

## `The best ways to perform some commonly desired tasks.`

## 

# **`Run Code at the Start of Levels`**

# 

`To generate levels, the game uses an object called GenCont.`  
`You can check if this object exists to figure out when a level finishes generating, like so:`

| \#define init 	global.level\_loading \= false; 	 \#define step	if(instance\_exists(GenCont) || instance\_exists(Menu)){		global.level\_loading \= true;	}	else if(global.level\_loading){		global.level\_loading \= false;		level\_start();	}	\#define level\_start	// code here runs at the start of every level |
| :---- |

`The above example also checks if Menu exists because the player can return to the character selection screen (controlled by Menu) at any time, like during a loading screen.`

`This example will not work outside of a .mod mod type, so for other mod types you can use wait:`

| \#define init 	global.level\_loading \= false; 	 	 // Manual Step Event: 	while(true){		if(instance\_exists(GenCont) || instance\_exists(Menu)){			global.level\_loading \= true;		}		else if(global.level\_loading){			global.level\_loading \= false;			level\_start();		} 		wait(0); 	}	\#define level\_start	// code here runs at the start of every level |
| :---- |

**`wait(0)`** `will always wait a single frame, which is important for Supporting Time Scales.`

# 

# **`Run Code on Newly Created Objects`**

# 

`The simplest way to find new objects is by checking for ones without a variable, and then setting it:`

| \#define step	with(instances\_matching(Bandit, "bluebandit\_check", null)){		bluebandit\_check \= true; 		image\_blend \= c\_blue;	} |
| :---- |

`Be careful though, because this runs constantly, adding a tiny bit of idle lag, and is pretty slow when an object has a lot of instances (like Wall, or enemy on high loops).`

`The best way to reduce the idle lag is as follows (friendly modders only):`

| \#define step 	if(instance\_exists(Bandit)){		var \_inst \= instances\_matching(Bandit, "bluebandit\_check", null); 		if(array\_length(\_inst)){ 			with(\_inst){				bluebandit\_check \= true; 				image\_blend \= c\_blue;			}		}	} |
| :---- |

`If necessary, the absolute fastest way (on average) to fetch new objects is to take advantage of the id variable being incremental:`

| \#define init 	global.bandit\_search\_id \= instance\_max; 	 \#define step 	if(instance\_exists(Bandit) && Bandit.id \> global.bandit\_search\_id){ 		with(instances\_matching\_gt(Bandit, "id", global.bandit\_search\_id)){ 			image\_blend \= c\_blue;		} 		global.bandit\_search\_id \= instance\_max;	} 	 \#macro instance\_max 	instance\_create(0, 0, DramaCamera) // destroys itself instantly, good for getting the latest id |
| :---- |

`Conveniently, this method can also capture instances created by the function instance_copy.`

`If you don’t want your code to be delayed by a frame, see Intercepting Events.`

# 

# **`Run Code on Destroyed/Killed Objects`**

# 

`There are two main ways to determine when an object gets destroyed: Prediction and Storage.`

**`Prediction`** `involves checking an object’s destruction condition(s) before they do. For example, to run code on a Bandit about to die, you can check if their my_health is <= 0, like so:`

| \#define step 	with(instances\_matching\_le(Bandit, "my\_health", 0)){ 		instance\_create(x, y, SmallExplosion); 	} |
| :---- |

`Just to note, the .mod step event is the best place to check for enemy death, because:`

* `The .mod step event runs from MiscCont’s begin step event.`  
* `Enemies check their health and destroy themselves in their step event.`  
* `Almost all damage is dealt during collision events.`


  `(See: Event Order)`


  `Furthermore, the .mod step event will not work for predicting prop deaths, because props check health and are destroyed in their begin step event. For this, you should use an end step event.`


  `Predicting if a Player is about to die would be more complicated, as they have more death conditions, like the candie variable, Strong Spirit, Chicken’s passive, Melting’s Skeleton transformation, etc. This might be a case where it’s easier to use the storage method.`


  **`Storage`** `involves remembering an instance (and any variables) until they no longer exist, for example:`


| \#define step 	if(instance\_exists(Player)){		var \_inst \= instances\_matching(Player, "gonnadielater\_check", null); 		if(array\_length(\_inst)){ 			with(\_inst){				gonnadielater\_check \= true; 				script\_bind\_step(follow\_player, 0, self);			}		}	} 	 \#define follow\_player(\_player) 	if(instance\_exists(\_player)){ 		x \= \_player.x; 		y \= \_player.y;	} 	else{ 		repeat(3){ 			instance\_create(x, y, Ally);		} 		instance\_destroy(); 	} |
| :---- |


  `For an explanation of script_bind_step, see Script Binding.`

# 

# **`Run Code on Hurt Objects`**

# 

`When a hitme object takes damage, it almost always:`

* `Loses HP          my_health -= _damage;`  
* `Gets pushed       motion_add(_direction, _force);`  
* `Sets i-frames     nexthurt = current_frame + 6;`  
* `Sets the sprite   sprite_index = spr_hurt; image_index = 0;`  
* `Plays a sound     sound_play_hit(snd_hurt, 0.2);`  
    
  `Checking any of these individually will lead to false positives, as none are unique to getting hurt. For example, MaggotSpawn (the nest) loses HP over time, the Player sets their sprite in portals, and many things can just set i-frames for invincibility.`  
    
  `The simplest way to check for hurt is to see if HP was lost and the hurt sprite is active, like so:`


| \#define step 	with(Player){ 		if(my\_health \< lsthealth && sprite\_index \== spr\_hurt){ 			if("mymod\_meat\_armor" not in self || mymod\_meat\_armor){ 				mymod\_meat\_armor \= false; 				instance\_create(x, y, MeatExplosion); 			}		} 		else mymod\_meat\_armor \= true;	} |
| :---- |


  `The lsthealth variable is Player-specific, but a custom variable can be used for other objects. Just make sure the variable’s name is unique so other mods don’t break it.`

# 

# **`Damage Hittable Objects`**

# 

`To damage a hitme object, one of the following functions can be used:`

| `Function` | `Description` |
| :---- | :---- |
| `projectile_hit(id, damage, ?force, ?direction)` | `Deals damage & optional knockback.` |
| `projectile_hit_push(id, damage, force)`  | `Deals damage & knockback away from self’s position, like an Explosion.` |
| `projectile_hit_np(id, damage, force, freeze)` | `Deals damage & knockback towards self’s direction. Adds freeze frames for hit Players.` |
| `projectile_hit_raw(id, damage, sndType)` | `Global Hit (Doesn’t pass self to hurt events). Deals damage & plays sound using sndType*: 0 = No Sound 1 = Normal Hurt Sound 2 = Heavy Hurt Sound * Custom on_hurt events override this.` |

`To check if a hitme object can be damaged by self, one of the following functions can be used:`

| `Function` | `Description` |
| :---- | :---- |
| `projectile_canhit(id)` | `Compares team.` |
| `projectile_canhit_melee(id)` | `Compares team & checks if id has i-frames.` |
| `projectile_canhit_np(id)` | `Compares team & checks if id’s HP is above 0. If id is a Player, checks if id has i-frames.` |

# 

# **`Draw Shadows`**

# 

`All hitme and chestprop objects have the variables spr_shadow, spr_shadow_x, and spr_shadow_y.`

**`spr_shadow`**   `- The shadow’s sprite index`  
**`spr_shadow_x`** `- The shadow’s x-offset from the hitme’s position`  
**`spr_shadow_y`** `- The shadow’s y-offset from the hitme’s position`

`For other situations, shadows are drawn in the .mod event draw_shadows, like so:`

| \#define draw\_shadows 	with(instances\_matching(Bullet1, "visible", true)){ 		draw\_sprite(shd24, 0, x, y); 	} |
| :---- |

`There are seven built-in shadow sprites: shd16, shd24, shd32, shd48, shd64, shd64B, and shd96. However, any sprite can be used as the game will automatically draw it in a flat color with low alpha.`

# 

# **`Draw Bloom`**

# 

`Bloom is drawn in the .mod event draw_bloom. Bloom is usually 2x scale and 0.1x alpha, like so:`

| \#define draw\_bloom 	with(instances\_matching(CustomProjectile, "name", "MyCoolProjectile")){		 		draw\_sprite\_ext( 			sprite\_index, 			image\_index, 			x, 			y, 			image\_xscale \* 2, 			image\_yscale \* 2, 			image\_angle, 			image\_blend, 			image\_alpha \* 0.1 		); 	} |
| :---- |

# 

# **`Break Walls`**

# 

`To break an individual Wall tile, use instance_destroy and make a FloorExplo at its position, like so:`

| with(instance\_nearest(10000, 10000, Wall)){ 	instance\_create(x, y, FloorExplo); 	instance\_destroy(); } |
| :---- |

`To destroy an area of Wall tiles, spawn a PortalClear and adjust its variables as needed, like so:`

| with(instance\_create(10016, 10016, PortalClear)){ 	image\_xscale \*= 2; 	image\_yscale \*= 2; } |
| :---- |

`By default, a PortalClear is an invisible circle with a radius of 32, and lasts 10 frames.`

# 

# **`Predict Collision`**

# 

`The Time Scale Guide and Event Guide sections may help in understanding this section.`

`Sometimes collision has to be predicted, as objects can get moved around or destroyed on collision.`  
`There are a few ways to predict collision, with various levels of accuracy and performance.`

`The simplest way to predict collision is to check ahead of an instance’s position using their speed.`  
`For example, if you wanted to know if the Player is about to run into a Wall, you can do:`

| with(Player){ 	if(place\_meeting(x \+ hspeed\_raw, y \+ vspeed\_raw, Wall)){ 		trace("WALLED\!");	}} |
| :---- |

`For best accuracy, predict collision in a real step event like script_bind_step, not .mod step.`

`This is pretty fast for Wall collision, but sometimes has false positives, and theoretically false negatives, because instances apply friction and gravity* to their speed before moving position.`  
`* gravity is rarely used, though.`

`For complete accuracy, this custom script motion_step lets you see where an instance is about to move:`

| with(Player){ 	motion\_step(1); 	if(place\_meeting(x, y, Wall)){ 		trace("WALLED\!");	} 	motion\_step(\-1);} \#define motion\_step(\_mult) 	/\* 		Performs the calling instance’s basic movement code, scaled by a given number 	\*/ 	 	if(\_mult \> 0){ 		if(friction\_raw \!= 0 && speed\_raw \!= 0){ 			speed\_raw \-= min(abs(speed\_raw), friction\_raw \* \_mult) \* sign(speed\_raw); 		} 		if(gravity\_raw \!= 0){ 			hspeed\_raw \+= lengthdir\_x(gravity\_raw, gravity\_direction) \* \_mult; 			vspeed\_raw \+= lengthdir\_y(gravity\_raw, gravity\_direction) \* \_mult; 		} 		if(speed\_raw \!= 0){ 			x \+= hspeed\_raw \* \_mult; 			y \+= vspeed\_raw \* \_mult; 		} 	} 	else{ 		if(speed\_raw \!= 0){ 			y \+= vspeed\_raw \* \_mult; 			x \+= hspeed\_raw \* \_mult; 		} 		if(gravity\_raw \!= 0){ 			vspeed\_raw \+= lengthdir\_y(gravity\_raw, gravity\_direction) \* \_mult; 			hspeed\_raw \+= lengthdir\_x(gravity\_raw, gravity\_direction) \* \_mult; 		} 		if(friction\_raw \!= 0 && speed\_raw \!= 0){ 			speed\_raw \-= min(abs(speed\_raw), friction\_raw \* \_mult) \* sign(speed\_raw); 		} 	} |
| :---- |

`This method is slightly slower, but should be entirely accurate since a normal Wall never moves.`

`However, it gets a little more intensive when both objects can move, like enemy and projectile:`

| with(projectile){ 	motion\_step(1); 	with(enemy){ 		motion\_step(1); 		if(place\_meeting(x, y, other)){ 			trace("HIT\!");		} 		motion\_step(\-1);	} 	motion\_step(\-1);} |
| :---- |

`As you can imagine, this would be pretty slow if checked constantly, particularly when there are a lot of enemy and projectile instances. However, it should be completely accurate.`

`One way to curb the lag is to cancel out early using instance_exists and distance_to_object, like so:`

| if(instance\_exists(projectile) && instance\_exists(enemy)){ 	var \_searchDis \= 16; 	with(projectile){ 		if(distance\_to\_object(enemy) \<= speed\_raw \+ \_searchDis){ 			motion\_step(1); 			if(distance\_to\_object(enemy) \<= \_searchDis){ 				with(enemy) if(distance\_to\_object(other) \<= \_searchDis){ 					motion\_step(1); 					if(place\_meeting(x, y, other)){ 						trace("HIT\!");					} 					motion\_step(\-1);				}			} 			motion\_step(\-1);		}	}} |
| :---- |

`While this has slightly worse accuracy, it is far faster. In this case, _searchDis is basically how fast an enemy can move without being able to bypass the collision check. Fortunately, an enemy moving that fast is incredibly unlikely. For example, an ExploFreak has a max speed of 3.`

`For further optimization, the custom script instances_meeting_rectangle can be used to replace:`

| with(enemy) if(distance\_to\_object(other) \<= \_searchDis){ |
| :---- |

`with the following:`

| with(instances\_meeting\_rectangle(x \- \_searchDis, y \- \_searchDis, x \+ \_searchDis, y \+ \_searchDis, enemy)){ |
| :---- |

# **`[ Weapon Guide ]`**

## `Tips related to weapons, see here for a guide on the .weapon mod format.`

## 

# **`Weapon Difficulty`**

# 

`The game’s difficulty starts at 1 and increments at each level transition. Difficulty is mainly used for determining enemy spawns and weapon drops.`

`A weapon’s area value determines the difficulty it starts spawning at. You might assume that an area value of 3 means it starts spawning on Desert-3, but in reality it translates to Desert-2. This is because the difficulty starts at 1 and weapon chests spawn guns from 1 difficulty ahead. However, guns dropped by enemies will be from the current difficulty, meaning 3 is only Desert-3 for enemy drops.`

`For reference, this chart from the wiki is based on weapon chest drops (Desert-1 = 2):`

[`![][image1]`](https://nuclear-throne.fandom.com/wiki/Weapons#Weapon_Chest_drops_table)

# 

# **`Firing Weapons`**

# 

`To fire a weapon held by a Player, you can use the function player_fire, like so:`

| \#define step 	with(Player){ 		if(button\_pressed(index, "horn")){ 			player\_fire();		}	} |
| :---- |

`Only calls firing code, includes no preliminary checks like if the Player has enough ammo.`

`To fire a weapon from a non-Player, you can use the function player_fire_ext, like so:`

| \#define step 	with(EnemyBullet1){ 		// gunangle, wep, x, y, team, creator, accuracy 		player\_fire\_ext(direction, wep\_plasma\_gun, x, y, team, creator, 1); 		instance\_delete(self);	} |
| :---- |

**`Warning:`** `Many modded weapons do not fully support player_fire_ext.`

# 

# **`Swapping Weapons`**

# 

`Swapping weapons is tedious, so you can use this custom script player_swap to automate the process:`

| with(Player){ 	player\_swap(true);} \#define player\_swap(\_FX) 	/\* 		Called from a Player to cycle their weapon slots, with optional swap FX 	\*/ 	 	with(\["%wep", "%curse", "%reload", "%wkick", "%wepflip", "%wepangle", "%can\_shoot", "%clicked", "%interfacepop", "drawempty%"\]){ 		var \_name \= \[string\_replace(self, "%", ""), string\_replace(self, "%", "b")\], 		    \_temp \= variable\_instance\_get(other, \_name\[0\], 0); 		     		variable\_instance\_set(other, \_name\[0\], variable\_instance\_get(other, \_name\[1\], 0)); 		variable\_instance\_set(other, \_name\[1\], \_temp);	} 	 	 // Effects: 	if(\_FX){ 		drawempty \= 30; 		swapmove  \= true; 		with(instance\_create(x, y, WepSwap)){ 			creator \= other; 		} 		 		 // Sound: 		if(weapon\_get\_gold(wep) \!= 0){ 			sound\_play(sndSwapGold); 		} 		if(curse \> 0){ 			sound\_play(sndSwapCursed); 		} 		sound\_play(weapon\_get\_swap(wep)); 	} |
| :---- |

# 

# **`Predicting Firing`**

# 

`To check if a Player is about to shoot their primary, you can use this custom macro player_will_fire:`

| \#macro player\_will\_fire 	/\* 		Used with a Player to check if they’re about to shoot their primary weapon 		Only works in the .mod, .skill, and .crown step events due to event order 	\*/ 	 	canfire 	&& can\_shoot \== true 	&& ( 		(ammo\[weapon\_get\_type(wep)\] \>= weapon\_get\_cost(wep) && GameCont.rad \>= weapon\_get\_rads(wep)) 		|| infammo \!= 0 	) 	&& ( 		((race \== "steroids") ? (weapon\_get\_auto(wep) \>= 0) : weapon\_get\_auto(wep)) 		? button\_check(index, "fire") 		: (clicked \== true || (button\_pressed(index, "fire") && reload \< 15)) 	) 	&& visible 	&& \!instance\_exists(GenCont) 	&& \!instance\_exists(LevCont) 	&& \!instance\_exists(PlayerSit) 	&& \!array\_length(instances\_matching(CrystalShield, "creator", self)) 	 \#define step 	 // \+2 Side Shots: 	with(Player){ 		if(player\_will\_fire){ 			for(var \_ang \= \-45; \_ang \<= 45 && player\_will\_fire; \_ang \+= 90){ 				player\_fire(gunangle \+ \_ang); 				can\_shoot \= true; 				clicked   \= true; 			}		}	} |
| :---- |

`This macro only works properly in the .mod, .skill, and .crown step events.`

# 

# **`Custom Blood Weapons`**

# 

`To make a custom weapon use HP when out of ammo, the following code can be used in the weapon file:`

| \#define step(\_primary) 	var \_wep \= (\_primary ? wep : bwep); 	 	 // Blood for Ammo: 	if(infammo \== 0){ 		if( 			\_primary 			? (drawempty  \== 30 && canfire && button\_pressed(index, "fire")) 			: (drawemptyb \== 30 && canspec && button\_pressed(index, "spec") && race \== "steroids") 		){ 			var \_type \= weapon\_get\_type(\_wep), 			    \_cost \= weapon\_get\_cost(\_wep); 			     			if(ammo\[\_type\] \< \_cost){ 				ammo\[\_type\] \+= \_cost; 				 				 // Damage: 				var \_damage \= floor(sqrt(\_cost)); 				lasthit \= \[weapon\_get\_sprt(\_wep), weapon\_get\_name(\_wep)\]; 				projectile\_hit\_raw(self, \_damage, 1); 				sound\_play\_hit(sndBloodHurt, 0.1); 				sleep(40); 				 				 // Insta-Use Ammo: 				if(\_primary && can\_shoot \== true){ 					clicked \= true; 				} 			} 		} 	} |
| :---- |

# 

# **`Custom Burst Weapons`**

# 

`There is no built-in support for burst weapons, so one way to make them is to create a controller object that uses an alarm to handle the firing.`

`The following can be used as a basic template:`

| \#define weapon\_fire 	var \_creator \= ( 		(instance\_is(self, FireCont) && "creator" in self) 		? creator 		: self 	); 	 	 // Burst Controller: 	with(instance\_create(x, y, CustomObject)){ 		gunangle \= other.gunangle; 		accuracy \= other.accuracy; 		team     \= other.team; 		creator  \= \_creator; 		alarm0   \= 1; 		ammo     \= 3; 		on\_step  \= burst\_step; 		event\_perform(ev\_step, ev\_step\_normal); 	} 	 \#define burst\_step 	if(alarm0 \>= 0 && \--alarm0 \== 0){ 		if(ammo \> 0 && instance\_exists(creator)){ 			ammo--; 			alarm0 \= 2; 			 			 // Update Vars: 			x \= creator.x; 			y \= creator.y; 			if("gunangle" in creator){ 				gunangle \= creator.gunangle; 			} 			 			 // Projectile: 			with(instance\_create(x, y, Bullet1)){ 				speed       \= 16; 				direction   \= other.gunangle \+ (random\_range(\-2, 2) \* other.accuracy); 				image\_angle \= direction; 				projectile\_init(other.team, other.creator); 			} 		} 		else instance\_destroy(); 	} |
| :---- |

# 

# **`Custom Charge Weapons`**

# 

`One way to make a custom charge weapon that fires on-release is to use Lightweight Object Weapons and a controller object that waits for the weapon to stop being fired.`

`The following can be used as a basic template:`

| \#define weapon\_sprt  return sprSlugger; \#define weapon\_cost  return 0; \#define weapon\_load  return 30; \#define weapon\_auto  return true; \#define weapon\_melee return false; \#define weapon\_chrg  return true;  \#define weapon\_fire(\_wep) 	var \_creator \= ( 		(instance\_is(self, FireCont) && "creator" in self) 		? creator 		: self 	); 	 	 // Setup LWO: 	if(\!is\_object(\_wep)){ 		\_wep \= { "wep" : \_wep }; 		if("wep" in \_creator && \_creator.wep \== \_wep.wep){ 			\_creator.wep \= \_wep; 		} 	} 	 	 // 1 Frame Reload: 	var \_load \= variable\_instance\_get(\_creator, "reloadspeed", 1) \* current\_time\_scale; 	reload \= min(reload, \_load); 	 	 // Charge Controller: 	if("cont" not in \_wep || \!instance\_exists(\_wep.cont) || \_wep.cont.creator \!= \_creator){ 		\_wep.cont \= instance\_create(x, y, CustomObject); 		with(\_wep.cont){ 			creator \= \_creator; 			wep     \= \_wep; 			charge  \= 0; 			on\_step \= charge\_step; 		} 	} 	with(\_wep.cont){ 		 // Update Vars: 		gunangle \= other.gunangle; 		accuracy \= other.accuracy; 		team     \= other.team; 		primary  \= \!(other.race \== "steroids" && "specfiring" in other && other.specfiring); 		 		 // Keep Charging: 		charging \= true; 		charge \+= \_load; 	} 	 	 // Charging FX: 	weapon\_post(-sqrt(\_wep.cont.charge), sqrt(\_wep.cont.charge), 0); 	 \#define charge\_step 	if(charging){ 		charging \= false; 	} 	else{ 		if(instance\_exists(creator)){ 			if(variable\_instance\_get(creator, (primary ? "wep" : "bwep"), wep) \== wep){ 				 // Update Vars: 				x \= creator.x; 				y \= creator.y; 				if("gunangle" in creator){ 					gunangle \= creator.gunangle; 				} 				 				 // Set Reload: 				if(primary){ 					if("reload"    in creator) creator.reload   \+= weapon\_get\_load(wep); 					if("can\_shoot" in creator) creator.can\_shoot \= false; 				} 				else{ 					if("breload"    in creator) creator.breload   \+= weapon\_get\_load(wep); 					if("bcan\_shoot" in creator) creator.bcan\_shoot \= false; 				} 				 				 // Projectile: 				with(instance\_create(x, y, Slug)){ 					speed       \= other.charge / 2; 					direction   \= other.gunangle \+ (random\_range(\-8, 8) \* other.accuracy); 					image\_angle \= direction; 					projectile\_init(other.team, other.creator); 				} 			} 		} 		instance\_destroy(); 	} |
| :---- |

`The custom script weapon_chrg is only for mod synergy. For example, Defpack 4.0 adds an icon to a weapon’s pick-up prompt if it returns true for weapon_chrg.`

# 

# **`Supporting player_fire_ext`**

# 

`To shoot guns from a non-Player, the game uses the FireCont object, which pretends to be a Player.`

`Unfortunately, FireCont only has a few Player variables, and all player_fire_ext calls use one main FireCont. This means that complex custom guns will require some manual support for player_fire_ext.`

`The only variables that can be referenced normally in the weapon_fire event must be shared by both Player and FireCont, or the gun will ERROR with player_fire_ext. Currently, these variables are:`

> > > * **`gunangle`**  
> > > * **`wepangle`**  
> > > * **`accuracy`**  
> > > * **`wkick`**  
> > > * **`team`**  
> > > * **`race`**  
> > > * **`index`**  
> > > * **`right`**  
> > > * **`reload`**  
> > > * **`infammo`**  
> > > * **`can_shoot`**  
> > > * **`specfiring`** `(Only in NTT versions 9941+)`  
> > > * `Any default variable, like x, y, speed, etc.`


  `If referencing any other variable, check for it in the creator, as seen with curse and wep here:`


| \#define weapon\_fire(\_wep) 	var \_creator \= ( 		(instance\_is(self, FireCont) && "creator" in self) 		? creator 		: self 	); 	 	 // Cursed, Randomize: 	if("curse" in \_creator && \_creator.curse \> 0){ 		if("wep" in \_creator && \_creator.wep \== \_wep){ 			\_creator.wep \= choose(wep\_disc\_gun, wep\_toxic\_launcher, wep\_toxic\_bow); 		} 	} |
| :---- |


  `Furthermore, since the same FireCont is used for every player_fire_ext call, store variables needed for later, and update them using the creator if necessary, as seen in the Custom Burst Weapon example.`


  `It helps to set any creator variables to FireCont’s creator, like so:`


| \#define weapon\_fire 	var \_creator \= ( 		(instance\_is(self, FireCont) && "creator" in self) 		? creator 		: self 	); 	 	 // Projectile: 	with(instance\_create(x, y, Bullet1)){ 		speed       \= 16; 		direction   \= other.gunangle \+ (random\_range(\-2, 2) \* other.accuracy); 		image\_angle \= direction; 		projectile\_init(other.team, \_creator); 	} |
| :---- |


  `Unfortunately, FireCont’s creator variable isn’t accessible in NTT versions 9940 and below, so checking if the variable exists first is necessary.`


  **`Note: projectile_init`** `just sets the team and creator, and also offsets projectiles on low time scales so they don’t break instantly when fired next to a Wall.`

# 

# **`[ Camera Guide ]`**

## `How to move the camera around.`

## 

# **`Setting the Camera’s Target`**

# 

`To make a player’s camera follow a custom target, set view_object[index] to an instance, like so:`

| for(var i \= 0; i \< maxp; i\++){ 	view\_object\[i\] \= instance\_nearest(10016, 10016, enemy); } |
| :---- |

**`view_object`** `does not work at the character selection screen or during the game over cutscene.`

`To reset the camera’s target to the default, set view_object[index] = noone.`

# 

# **`Setting the Camera’s Mouse Pan`**

# 

`To set the mouse pan of a player’s camera, set view_pan_factor[index] to a number, like so:`

| for(var i \= 0; i \< maxp; i\++){ 	view\_pan\_factor\[i\] \= 2; } |
| :---- |

`The default mouse pan is equivalent to 4, bolt weapons use 3, and melee weapons use 8.`  
`To disable the mouse pan, you can use a really high number like 9999.`

`To reset the camera’s mouse pan to the default, set view_pan_factor[index] = undefined. This will also happen between levels automatically.`

# 

# **`Setting the Camera’s Zoom`**

# 

`To set the dimensions of all player cameras, set game_width and game_height, like so:`

| game\_width  \= 640; game\_height \= 480; |
| :---- |

`There is no way to set the dimensions of an individual player’s camera, only for all players.`

`To reset the camera’s dimensions to the default, set game_width = 320 and game_height = 240.`

# 

# **`Screenshake`**

# 

`Screenshake is normally made using the functions view_shake_at and view_shake_max_at. These will apply screenshake to all cameras, based on the distance from the given position to the screen.`

| view\_shake\_at(x, y, 10); |
| :---- |

**`view_shake_max_at`** `is the same as view_shake_at, except overall screenshake won’t go over the given amount.`

**`view_shake[index]`** `is the overall screenshake value of a player’s camera.`

# 

# **`[ HUD Guide ]`**

## `How to toggle HUD elements and draw custom HUD with co-op support.`

## 

# **`Setting HUD Visibility`**

# 

`The following functions exist for setting the visibility of certain HUD elements:`

| `Function` | `Description` |
| :---- | :---- |
| `player_set_show_hud(playerA, playerB, show)` | `Sets the visibility of player A’s main HUD for player B (HP, weapons, ammo, etc.).` |
| `player_set_show_prompts(playerA, playerB, show)` | `Sets the visibility of player A’s prompts for player B (weapon pickups, YV’s car, etc.).` |
| `player_set_show_marker(playerA, playerB, show)` | `Sets the visibility of player A’s co-op & chat markers for player B (P1, P2, etc.).` |
| `player_set_show_cursor(playerA, playerB, show)`  | `Sets the visibility of player A’s cursor for player B.` |
| `player_set_show_skills(player, show)` | `Sets the visibility of mutation HUD for the given player.` |

`Each function has a _get variant for fetching the visibility, like player_get_show_hud(A, B).`

# 

# **`Custom Player HUD`**

# 

`Drawing custom HUD elements is as simple as normal drawing, and at minimum requires an offset by the screen’s position. This can be done using the .mod event draw_gui, the function draw_set_projection (see api.gml), or the variables view_xview and view_yview (or their _nonsync alternatives).`

`However, there are a few things that can be tricky to support, such as co-op, the game-win fade-out, and the pause screen. The following code can be used to automatically support co-op and the fade-out:`

| \#define player\_hud(\_player, \_hudIndex, \_hudSide) 	 // Portal Strike Ammo: 	draw\_sprite\_ext( 		(ultra\_get("rogue", 1) ? sprRogueAmmoHUDTB : sprRogueAmmoHUD), 		\_player.rogueammo, 		(\_hudSide ? 1 : 93), 		4, 		(\_hudSide ? \-1 : 1), 		1, 		0, 		c\_white, 		1 	); 	 	 // Character Icon: 	draw\_sprite(\_player.sprite\_index, 0.4 \* current\_frame, 8, 10); 	 \#define draw\_gui 	 // Player HUD Management: 	if(instance\_exists(Player) && \!instance\_exists(PopoScene) && \!instance\_exists(MenuGen)){ 		if(instance\_exists(TopCont) || instance\_exists(GenCont) || instance\_exists(LevCont)){ 			var \_hudFade  \= 0, 			    \_hudIndex \= 0, 			    \_lastSeed \= random\_get\_seed(); 			     			 // Game Win Fade Out: 			if(array\_length(instances\_matching(TopCont, "fadeout", true))){ 				with(TopCont){ 					\_hudFade \= clamp(fade, 0, 1); 				} 			} 			if(\_hudFade \> 0){ 				 // GMS1 Partial Fix: 				try if(\!null){} 				catch(\_error){ 					\_hudFade \= min(\_hudFade, round(\_hudFade)); 				} 				 				 // Dim Drawing: 				if(\_hudFade \> 0){ 					draw\_set\_fog(true, c\_black, 0, 16000 / \_hudFade); 				} 			} 			 			 // Draw Player HUD: 			for(var \_isOnline \= 0; \_isOnline \<= 1; \_isOnline\++){ 				for(var \_index \= 0; \_index \< maxp; \_index\++){ 					if( 						player\_is\_active(\_index) 						&& (\_hudIndex \< 2 || \!instance\_exists(LevCont)) 						&& (player\_is\_local\_nonsync(\_index) ^^ \_isOnline) 					){ 						var \_hudVisible \= false; 						 						 // HUD Visibility: 						for(var i \= 0; true; i\++){ 							var \_local \= player\_find\_local\_nonsync(i); 							if(\!player\_is\_active(\_local)){ 								break; 							} 							if(player\_get\_show\_hud(\_index, \_local)){ 								\_hudVisible \= true; 								break; 							} 						} 						 						 // Draw HUD: 						if(\_hudVisible || \_isOnline \== 0){ 							if(\_hudVisible){ 								var \_player \= player\_find(\_index); 								if(instance\_exists(\_player)){ 									 // Rad Canister / Co-op Offsets: 									var \_playerNum \= 0; 									for(var i \= 0; i \< maxp; i\++){ 										\_playerNum \+= player\_is\_active(i); 									} 									if(\_playerNum \<= 1){ 										d3d\_set\_projection\_ortho( 											view\_xview\_nonsync \- 17, 											view\_yview\_nonsync, 											game\_width, 											game\_height, 											0 										); 									} 									else draw\_set\_projection(2, \_index); 									 									 // Draw: 									player\_hud(\_player, \_hudIndex, \_hudIndex % 2); 									 									draw\_reset\_projection(); 								} 							} 							\_hudIndex\++; 						} 					} 				} 			} 			if(\_hudFade \> 0){ 				draw\_set\_fog(false, 0, 0, 0); 			} 			random\_set\_seed(\_lastSeed); 		} 	} |
| :---- |

`The script player_hud is where custom HUD elements can be drawn. This script is called for each player, and also aligns any drawn elements to the top left of their health bar automatically.`

`The arguments of the player_hud script are:`

**`player`**   `- The Player instance whose HUD is being drawn, for referencing variables.`  
**`hudIndex`** `- The index of the player’s HUD, 0=Top Left, 1=Top Right, 2=Bottom Left, etc.`   
**`hudSide`**  `- If the player’s HUD is on the left side of the screen (false) or right (true).`

`This code will only work in a .mod file, as it uses the draw_gui event.`

**`Warning:`** `Do not set any non-local variables or create/destroy any instances in the player_hud script, or else the mod will likely cause a desync in online co-op.`

`The above code does not support pause screen HUD, so the following can be appended to it for that:`

| \#define draw\_pause 	 // Paused Player HUD Management: 	var \_local \= player\_find\_local\_nonsync(); 	if(player\_is\_active(\_local)){ 		 // Store Main Player’s Variables: 		if(instance\_exists(Player)){ 			global.hud\_pause\_vars \= undefined; 			with(player\_find(\_local)){ 				global.hud\_pause\_vars \= {}; 				with(variable\_instance\_get\_names(self)){ 					lq\_set(global.hud\_pause\_vars, self, variable\_instance\_get(other, self)); 				} 			} 		} 		 		 // Draw Main Player’s HUD: 		if(\!instance\_exists(BackMainMenu)){ 			var \_ref  \= script\_ref\_create(draw\_pause), 			    \_vars \= mod\_variable\_get(\_ref\[0\], \_ref\[1\], "hud\_pause\_vars"); 			     			if(\!is\_undefined(\_vars)){ 				for(var i \= 0; player\_is\_active(player\_find\_local\_nonsync(i)); i\++){ 					if(player\_get\_show\_hud(\_local, player\_find\_local\_nonsync(i))){ 						var \_playerNum \= 0, 						    \_lastSeed  \= random\_get\_seed(); 						     						 // View \+ Rad Canister Offset: 						for(var i \= 0; i \< maxp; i\++){ 							\_playerNum \+= player\_is\_active(i); 						} 						d3d\_set\_projection\_ortho( 							((\_playerNum \<= 1) ? \-17 : 0), 							0, 							game\_width, 							game\_height, 							0 						); 						 						 // Draw: 						player\_hud(global.hud\_pause\_vars, 0, false); 						 						draw\_reset\_projection(); 						random\_set\_seed(\_lastSeed); 						break; 					} 				} 			} 		} 	} |
| :---- |

`Since Player instances are deactivated on the pause screen, this stores the main Player’s variables in a Lightweight Object right before the game is paused, and uses it for the HUD.`

`Along with the first example, this only works in a .mod file, as it uses the draw_pause event.`

# 

# **`[ Time Scale Guide ]`**

## `How to make a mod compatible with 60 FPS, slow motion, etc.`

## 

# **`What Is Time Scaling?`**

# 

`Since Nuclear Throne was coded to be a 30 FPS game, setting the room_speed to any other value only changes how often the game runs its events. For example, setting room_speed to 60 would make the game play at 2x speed, because all game logic is just running twice as often per second (60 / 30 = 2).`

`As such, the variable current_time_scale was implemented, which is a multiplier used to slow down all continuously-running code. For 60 FPS, room_speed is set to 60 to make game code run twice as often, and current_time_scale is set to 0.5 to halve the rate of change.`

# 

# **`Supporting Time Scales`**

# 

`First, keep in mind that time scaling should only be applied to continuous operations. In other words, any code that runs every frame or can run multiple frames in a row, and affects code on future frames. For example, code running in a step event or collision event.`

`Most manual time scale support is just multiplying a value by current_time_scale, like so:`

| \#define step 	with(Player){ 		// x \+= 4 \* sin(current\_frame / 5\) 		x \+= 4 \* sin(current\_frame / 5) \* current\_time\_scale; 		 		// if(random(5) \< 2){ 		// 	instance\_create(x, y, Smoke) 		// } 		if(random(5) \< 2 \* current\_time\_scale){ 			instance\_create(x, y, Smoke);		}	} |
| :---- |

`For exponential changes, values should be raised to the power of current_time_scale, like so:`

| \#define step 	with(Corpse){ 		// image\_alpha \*= 0.95 		image\_alpha \*= power(0.95, current\_time\_scale);	} 	with(FlakBullet){ 		if(speed \< 10){ 			// speed \= power(speed, 1.5) 			speed \= power(speed, power(1.5, current\_time\_scale));		}	} |
| :---- |

# 

`If there isn’t a way to adjust the rate of change, you can just make code play once every full frame:`

| \#macro current\_frame\_active 	(current\_frame % 1) \< current\_time\_scale 	 \#define step 	if(current\_frame\_active){ 		with(projectile){ 			instance\_create(x \+ random\_range(\-4, 4), y \+ random\_range(\-4, 4), PlasmaTrail);		}	} |
| :---- |

**`current_frame_active`** `doesn’t support time scales above 1, because this is largely unnecessary. However, the following could be done to support all time scales:`

| \#macro current\_frame\_repeat 	((current\_frame % 1) \< (current\_time\_scale % 1)) 	? ceil(current\_time\_scale) 	: floor(current\_time\_scale) 	 \#define step 	var i \= current\_frame\_repeat; 	if(i) repeat(i){ 		with(projectile){ 			instance\_create(x \+ random\_range(\-4, 4), y \+ random\_range(\-4, 4), PlasmaTrail);		}	} |
| :---- |

`All base game systems support time scaling automatically. The moment current_time_scale is set, each instance adjusts its image_speed, speed, hspeed, vspeed, friction, and gravity accordingly. On the mod’s side these variables don’t appear to change, but their raw variants do (image_speed_raw, speed_raw, hspeed_raw, vspeed_raw, friction_raw, gravity_raw). Each raw variable is an alias for the actual variable; so, if speed is 10 and current_time_scale is 0.2, speed_raw is 2.`

`Alarms also support time scaling, but slightly differently. Every (1 / current_time_scale) - 1 frames, all alarms above 0 will be incremented by 1. Currently, alarms do not support time scales over 1.`

# 

# **`Quick Reference`** 

# 

| `Normal` | `Continuous (w/ Time Scaling) ts = current_time_scale` |
| :---- | :---- |
| `a += b` | `a += b * ts` |
| `a -= b` | `a -= b * ts` |
| `a *= b` | `a *= power(b, ts)` |
| `a /= b` | `a /= power(b, ts)` |
| `a = lerp(a, b, amount)` | `a = lerp(b, a, power(1 - amount, ts))` |
| `a = merge_color(a, b, amount)` | `a = merge_color(b, a, power(1 - amount, ts))` |
| `a = a + (angle_difference(b, a) * amount)` | `a = b + (angle_difference(a, b) * power(1 - amount, ts))` |
| `if(random(a) < b)` | `if(random(a) < b * ts)` |
| `if((a % interval) == 0)` | `if((a % interval) < ts)` |
| `motion_add(direction, speed)` | `motion_add_ct(direction, speed)` |

# 

# **`[ Event Guide ]`**

## `Tips related to GameMaker’s event system.`

## 

# **`Event Order`**

`GameMaker documentation states that the event order is mostly a secret, and you shouldn't rely on it for your game to function properly as it could be changed later. This makes sense for creating a game, but for NTT modding it's crucial to know the event order if you want to intercept base game code.`

`Notes`

`The game goes through every instance per event (not every event per instance).`  
`Objects created during an event do not run that event on the same frame.`  
`Setting depth during a draw event has no effect on drawing priority until the next frame.`

`General Event Order`  
`Normal game code runs here.`

	`Per event, loops through:`  
`Objects (0 → max)`  
`Instances (oldest → newest)`  
	

> > > 1. `Sets xprevious,yprevious to x,y`  
> > > 2. [`Animation`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/002_reference/objects%20and%20instances/instances/instance%20properties/image_speed.html)  
> > > 3. [`Begin Step`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/step%20event.html) `(.mod step event runs from MiscCont Begin Step)`  
> > > 4. [`Alarms`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/alarm%20event.html) `(12 Separate Events)`  
> > > 5. [`Step`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/step%20event.html)  
> > > 6. [`Movement`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/002_reference/movement%20and%20collisions/movement/index.html)  
> > > 7. [`Collision`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/collision%20event.html)  
> > > 8. [`End Step`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/step%20event.html)  
   	  
   `Drawing Event Order`  
   `These play after the general events.`  
     
   	`Per event, loops through:`

   **`depth`** `(highest → lowest)`

   `Instances with the most recently updated depth (newest → oldest)`

   	  
> > > 1. [`Pre Draw`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/pre%20and%20post%20draw%20event.html)  
> > > 2. [`Draw Begin`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/draw%20event.html)  
> > > 3. [`Draw`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/draw%20event.html)  
> > > 4. [`Draw End`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/draw%20event.html)  
> > > 5. [`Post Draw`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/pre%20and%20post%20draw%20event.html)  
> > > 6. [`Draw GUI Begin`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/draw%20gui%20event.html)  
> > > 7. [`Draw GUI`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/draw%20gui%20event.html)  
> > > 8. [`Draw GUI End`](https://docs.yoyogames.com/source/dadiospice/000_using%20gamemaker/events/draw%20gui%20event.html)

# 

# **`Intercepting Events`**

# 

`Knowing the Event Order, you can put your code in the right place to do some useful things.`

`For example, say you have some code to buff the damage of newly created player projectiles. If this code runs in the .mod step event, its effect will be delayed by 1 frame because:`

> > > 1. `Almost all objects shoot projectiles during an alarm event or their step event.`  
> > > 2. `The .mod step event is called from MiscCont’s begin step event.`

   

   `This means that player projectiles will at least run movement, collision, drawing, and animation code before getting buffed. So, if the player shoots at an enemy point-blank, they won’t deal extra damage.`

   

   `To fix this, you can use the script_bind_step function to run your code in a real step event, like so:`

   

| \#define init 	global.bind\_step \= noone; 	 \#define cleanup 	 // Unbind Script on Mod Unload: 	with(global.bind\_step){ 		instance\_destroy(); 	} 	 \#define step 	 // Bind 'post\_step' Script to a Step Event: 	if(\!instance\_exists(global.bind\_step)){ 		global.bind\_step \= script\_bind\_step(post\_step, 0); 	} 	 \#define post\_step 	 // Increase Player Damage by 1: 	if(instance\_exists(projectile)){		var \_inst \= instances\_matching(projectile, "playerdamagebuff\_check", null); 		if(array\_length(\_inst)){			with(\_inst){				playerdamagebuff\_check \= true; 				if(instance\_is(creator, Player)){ 					damage++; 				} 			} 		}	} |
| :---- |

   

   `Conveniently, the CustomScript object and its children all have the highest object indices, so their general events will run after all other objects (except MiscCont and CorpseActive).`

# 

# **`[ Optimization Guide ]`**

## `The most effective ways to improve a mod’s performance.`

## 

# **`General Tips`**

# 

`Nuclear Throne Together mods can be pretty slow, although GMS2 versions (9942+) speed them up greatly. All modded code is interpreted by the game, making it inherently slower than normal GML code.`

`For optimization, the best thing to keep in mind is that you want to run as few operations as possible. If you can reduce how much code runs and still achieve the same effect, do that. If you can make the game itself perform a task for you, do that.`

`One way to reduce the intensity of code without changing its effect is to store information for later.`  
`For example, to loop over an array, you can store its size instead of constantly calling array_length:`

`Original:`

| var \_list \= \[1, 2, 3\]; for(var i \= 0; i \< array\_length(\_list); i\++){ 	trace(\_list\[i\]); } |
| :---- |

`Faster (no longer calls array_length every time the limit is checked):`

| var \_list \= \[1, 2, 3\],     \_size \= array\_length(\_list);      for(var i \= 0; i \< \_size; i\++){ 	trace(\_list\[i\]); } |
| :---- |

`Also faster, but runs in reverse which won’t work for everything:`

| var \_list \= \[1, 2, 3\]; for(var i \= array\_length(\_list) \- 1; i \>= 0; i\--){ 	trace(\_list\[i\]); } |
| :---- |

**`SECRET PRO TIP:`** `You can use with to loop over an array like a for-each.`  
`This is fastest, because the game is looping over the array for you:`

| var \_list \= \[1, 2, 3\]; with(\_list){ 	trace(self); } |
| :---- |

`Another way to improve performance is to stop execution early when possible. For example, to make an enemy absorb any Rad pickups that it touches, you can check if both objects exist in the first place:`

`Original:`

| with(enemy){ 	if(place\_meeting(x, y, Rad)){ 		raddrop++; 		with(Rad){ 			if(place\_meeting(x, y, other)){ 				instance\_destroy(); 			} 		} 	} } |
| :---- |

`Faster (no longer loops over enemy instances when it would be pointless to):`

| if(instance\_exists(enemy) && instance\_exists(Rad)){ 	with(enemy){ 		if(place\_meeting(x, y, Rad)){ 			raddrop++; 			with(Rad){ 				if(place\_meeting(x, y, other)){ 					instance\_destroy(); 				} 			} 		} 	} } |
| :---- |

`Another great way to keep code fast is to use built-in systems whenever possible. For example, it is much faster (and easier) to use array_sort or array_sort_sub than to sort an array manually, as the sorting is done internally. Similarly, it is much faster to use a resprited Wind, BulletHit, or other Effect object for custom effects, as opposed to coding them from scratch.`

`To keep this short, remember that all of the above concepts can be applied very broadly.`

# 

# **`Troubleshooting Lag`**

# 

`To see how much real time it takes to execute a chunk of code, your best friend is trace_time.`

**`trace_time`** `is like trace, except it also prints the number of microseconds that have passed since trace_time was last called. It is used as follows:`

| trace\_time(); // code goes here trace\_time("lag"); |
| :---- |

`The time it takes can vary wildly, so test multiple times to get an idea of the average.`

`When optimizing, it also helps to run code multiple times, like so:`

| trace\_time(); repeat(100){ 	// code goes here } trace\_time("lag"); |
| :---- |

`This makes it easier to see if a change has sped up or slowed down the code.`

`To write your own lag-tracing implementation, you can use get_timer_nonsync. For example, to automatically determine the average microseconds that it takes to run a piece of code, you can do:`

| \#define init 	global.num \= 0; 	global.tot \= 0; 	 \#define step 	var i \= get\_timer\_nonsync(); 	// code goes here 	global.num \+= get\_timer\_nonsync() \- i; 	global.tot++; 	trace(global.num / global.tot); |
| :---- |

`The game has about 33,333 microseconds to work with per frame before the FPS begins to dip, as the game runs at 30 FPS and there are 1,000,000 microseconds in a second (1,000,000 / 30 = ~33,333). For this reason, try to keep your code’s execution time far below this number, as it stacks with the execution time of other mods and the base game.`

# 

# **`instances_matching`**

`One of the best functions for boosting performance is called instances_matching.`

`Basically, instances_matching is a much faster version of checking with(object) if(variable == value).`

`Original:`

| with(WepPickup) if(wep \== wep\_shotgun){ 	wep \= wep\_slugger; } |
| :---- |

`Faster:`

| with(instances\_matching(WepPickup, "wep", wep\_shotgun)){ 	wep \= wep\_slugger; } |
| :---- |

`To check more values, you can add more arguments, like so:`

| with(instances\_matching(WepPickup, "wep", wep\_shotgun, wep\_crossbow, wep\_wrench)){ 	wep \= wep\_slugger; } |
| :---- |

`To check more objects, the first argument can be an array, like so:`

| with(instances\_matching(\[WepPickup, Player, ThrownWep\], "wep", wep\_shotgun)){ 	wep \= wep\_slugger; } |
| :---- |

`There are six forms of instances_matching, one for each of the following comparison operators:`

| `Operator` | `Function Equivalent` |
| :---- | :---- |
| `==` | `instances_matching` |
| `!=` | `instances_matching_ne` |
| `<` | `instances_matching_lt` |
| `>` | `instances_matching_gt` |
| `<=` | `instances_matching_le` |
| `>=` | `instances_matching_ge` |

`These functions can also be used to do a number of tasks incredibly quickly, for example:`

`Fetch a Random Instance (instance_find is currently broken):`

| \#define instance\_random(\_obj) 	/\* 		Returns a random instance of the given object(s) 	\*/ 	 	var \_inst \= instances\_matching(\_obj, "id", null), 	    \_size \= array\_length(\_inst); 	     	return ( 		(\_size \> 0) 		? \_inst\[irandom(\_size \- 1)\] 		: noone 	); |
| :---- |

`Faster point_in_rectangle Check:`

| \#define instances\_in\_rectangle(\_x1, \_y1, \_x2, \_y2, \_obj) 	/\* 		Returns all instances of the given object whose positions overlap the given rectangle 		Much better performance than checking 'point\_in\_rectangle()' on every instance 		 		Args: 			x1/y1/x2/y2 \- The rectangular area to search 			obj         \- The object(s) to search 	\*/ 	 	return ( 		instances\_matching\_le( 		instances\_matching\_le( 		instances\_matching\_ge( 		instances\_matching\_ge( 		\_obj, 		"x", \_x1), 		"y", \_y1), 		"x", \_x2), 		"y", \_y2) 	); |
| :---- |

`Faster collision_rectangle Check:`

| \#define instances\_meeting\_rectangle(\_x1, \_y1, \_x2, \_y2, \_obj) 	/\* 		Returns all instances of the given object whose bounding boxes overlap the given rectangle 		Much better performance than checking 'collision\_rectangle()' on every instance 		 		Args: 			x1/y1/x2/y2 \- The rectangular area to search 			obj         \- The object(s) to search 	\*/ 	 	return ( 		instances\_matching\_le( 		instances\_matching\_le( 		instances\_matching\_ge( 		instances\_matching\_ge( 		\_obj, 		"bbox\_right",  \_x1), 		"bbox\_bottom", \_y1), 		"bbox\_left",   \_x2), 		"bbox\_top",    \_y2) 	); |
| :---- |

`Faster position_meeting Check:`

| \#define instances\_meeting\_point(\_x, \_y, \_obj) 	/\* 		Returns all instances of the given object whose bounding boxes overlap the given position 		Much better performance than checking 'position\_meeting()' on every instance 		 		Args: 			x/y \- The position to search 			obj \- The object(s) to search 	\*/ 	 	return ( 		instances\_matching\_le( 		instances\_matching\_le( 		instances\_matching\_ge( 		instances\_matching\_ge( 		\_obj, 		"bbox\_right",  \_x), 		"bbox\_bottom", \_y), 		"bbox\_left",   \_x), 		"bbox\_top",    \_y) 	); |
| :---- |

`Faster place_meeting Check:`

| \#define instances\_meeting(\_x, \_y, \_obj) 	/\* 		Returns all instances of the given object whose bounding boxes overlap the calling instance's bounding box at the given position 		Much better performance than checking 'place\_meeting()' on every instance 		 		Args: 			x/y \- The position to search 			obj \- The object(s) to search 	\*/ 	 	var \_tx \= x, 	    \_ty \= y; 	     	x \= \_x; 	y \= \_y; 	 	var \_inst \= ( 		instances\_matching\_ne( 		instances\_matching\_le( 		instances\_matching\_le( 		instances\_matching\_ge( 		instances\_matching\_ge( 		\_obj, 		"bbox\_right",  bbox\_left), 		"bbox\_bottom", bbox\_top), 		"bbox\_left",   bbox\_right), 		"bbox\_top",    bbox\_bottom), 		"id",          id) 	); 	 	x \= \_tx; 	y \= \_ty; 		 	return \_inst; |
| :---- |

# **`Working With Limited Depth Values`**

`You can’t rely on a decimal depth, as depth can only be an integer in GMS2 NTT versions (9942+).`

`For instances with the same depth, the ones that most recently updated theirs will draw first.`  
`If you want to make an instance appear below all other instances of the same depth, you can do:`

| var \_depth \= depth; depth\++; if(fork()){ 	wait(0); 	if(instance\_exists(self) && depth \== \_depth \+ 1){ 		depth\--; 	} 	exit; } |
| :---- |

`Just depth++; depth--; works in GMS1 versions, but waiting a frame is required in GMS2 versions.`

#  **`[ Blend Mode Guide ]`**

## `Explaining GameMaker’s blend mode system.`

## 

# **`Blend Mode Basics`**

# 

`GameMaker's blend mode system is one of its most versatile tools for crafting visuals.`  
`So, if you like to make cool-looking stuff, it helps to know how to use them.`

`When the game draws pixels, there are source pixels and destination pixels.`  
`The source pixels are the ones you draw, like in a shape or sprite.`  
`The destination pixels are the canvas under the source pixels, like the screen (application surface).`  
`The blend mode determines the channel multipliers (red, green, blue, alpha) for these pixels.`

`Pixel blending involves two sets of channel multipliers, one for the source channels and one for the destination channels. The products of these channels are then added together.`

`To understand this process, see what happens when a bandit sprite is drawn onto a desert tile using the default source blend mode, bm_src_alpha, and the default destination blend mode, bm_inv_src_alpha:`

| `Initial` |  | `Initial Channels` | `Channel Multipliers` |  |  | `Channel Products` |  | `Final Product` |
| ----- | :---: | ----- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| `![][image2] Source` | **`➞`** | `![][image3]![][image4] ![][image5]![][image6]` | **`x`** | `![][image6]![][image6] ![][image6]![][image6]` | **`=`** | `![][image3]![][image4] ![][image5]![][image6]` | **`➞`** | `![][image7] Source` |
|  |  | **`➞ Blending Pipeline ➞`** |  |  |  |  |  | **`+`** |
| `![][image8] Destination` | **`➞`** | `![][image9]![][image10] ![][image11]![][image12]` | **`x`** | `![][image13]![][image13] ![][image13]![][image13]` | **`=`** | `![][image14]![][image15] ![][image16]![][image13]` | **`➞`** | `![][image17] Destination` |
|  |  | `Full black implies 0, RGB or white implies >0 to 1.` |  |  |  |  |  | **`=`** |
| `The Final Product column is just adding the channels together, like so: Final Red   = min(1, Source Red   + Destination Red) Final Green = min(1, Source Green + Destination Green) Final Blue  = min(1, Source Blue  + Destination Blue) Final Alpha = min(1, Source Alpha + Destination Alpha)` |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | `![][image18]` |

# 

# **`Blend Mode Reference`**

# 

`There are two functions for setting the blend mode, draw_set_blend_mode and draw_set_blend_mode_ext.`

**`draw_set_blend_mode_ext`** `uses the following constants for setting a custom blend mode:`

`The R Factor, G Factor, B Factor, and A Factor are the constant’s applied channel multipliers.`

`The S Product and D Product are the products of the source and destination pixels multiplied by the channel multipliers, as seen on the chart in the Blend Mode Basics section.`

| `Constant Name` | `R Factor` | `G Factor` | `B Factor` | `A Factor` | `S Product RGBA    RGB` | `D Product RGBA    RGB` |
| :---- | ----: | ----: | ----: | ----- | ----- | ----: |
| **`bm_zero`** | `0![][image19]` | `0![][image19]` | `0![][image19]` | `0![][image19]` | `![][image20]![][image19]` | `![][image20]![][image19]` |
| **`bm_one`** | `1![][image21]` | `1![][image21]` | `1![][image21]` | `1![][image21]` | `![][image22]![][image23]` | `![][image24]![][image25]` |
| **`bm_src_color`** | `Rs![][image3]` | `Gs![][image4]` | `Bs![][image5]` | `As![][image6]` | `![][image26]![][image27]` | `![][image28]![][image29]` |
| **`bm_inv_src_color`** | `1-Rs![][image30]` | `1-Gs![][image31]` | `1-Bs![][image32]` | `1-As![][image13]` | `![][image20]![][image33]` | `![][image34]![][image35]` |
| **`bm_src_alpha`** | `As![][image6]` | `As![][image6]` | `As![][image6]` | `As![][image6]` | `![][image22]![][image23]` | `![][image36]![][image37]` |
| **`bm_inv_src_alpha`** | `1-As![][image13]` | `1-As![][image13]` | `1-As![][image13]` | `1-As![][image13]` | `![][image20]![][image19]` | `![][image34]![][image38]` |
| **`bm_dest_color`** | `Rd![][image9]` | `Gd![][image10]` | `Bd![][image11]` | `Ad![][image12]` | `![][image28]![][image29]` | `![][image39]![][image40]` |
| **`bm_inv_dest_color`** | `1-Rd![][image41]` | `1-Gd![][image42]` | `1-Bd![][image43]` | `1-Ad![][image19]` | `![][image20]![][image44]` | `![][image20]![][image45]` |
| **`bm_dest_alpha`** | `Ad![][image12]` | `Ad![][image12]` | `Ad![][image12]` | `Ad![][image12]` | `![][image22]![][image23]` | `![][image24]![][image25]` |
| **`bm_inv_dest_alpha`** | `1-Ad![][image19]` | `1-Ad![][image19]` | `1-Ad![][image19]` | `1-Ad![][image19]` | `![][image20]![][image19]` | `![][image20]![][image19]` |
| **`bm_src_alpha_sat`** `f = min(As, 1-Ad)` | `f![][image19]` | `f![][image19]` | `f![][image19]` | `1![][image21]` | `![][image46]![][image19]` | `![][image47]![][image19]` |
| `* Full black implies 0, RGB or white implies >0 to 1. * Sprites trim empty borders, so in-game really uses ➞` |  |  |  | `![][image48]` | `* RGB-only images show any hidden color change.` |  |

**`draw_set_blend_mode`** `is a simpler version of draw_set_blend_mode_ext that uses these constants:`

**`bm_normal`**   `- Translates to (bm_src_alpha, bm_inv_src_alpha), the default blend mode.`  
**`bm_add`**      `- Translates to (bm_src_alpha, bm_one).`  
**`bm_subtract`** `- Translates to (bm_zero,      bm_inv_src_colour).`  
**`bm_max`**      `- Translates to (bm_src_alpha, bm_inv_src_colour).`

# **`[ Size Guide ]`**

## `Explaining the size variable in hitme objects.`

## 

`The size variable is used for a wide variety of things, such as corpse speed, death freeze frames, Melting’s corpse explosions, etc. Basically, anything related to how heavy a hittable object is.`

`For best results, follow this chart:`

| `0` | `Tiny` | `Maggot` |
| ----: | ----: | :---- |
| **`1`** | **`Basic Tiny Boss`** | `Bandit, Raven, SnowBot, Freak LilHunter` |
| **`*2`** | **`Medium`** | `Scorpion, SnowTank, RhinoFreak` |
| **`*3`** | **`Large Basic Boss`** | `Guardian, ExploGuardian BanditBoss, TechnoMancer` |
| **`4`** | **`Medium Boss`** | `ScrapBoss, FrogQueen, HyperCrystal` |
| **`5`** | **`Player`** | `Player, EnemyHorror` |
| **`🠗   6`** | **`Large Boss`** | `Throne, Throne2, Captain, Vans` |

`* Big Melting corpse explosions if above size 1.`  
`* Can't be hurt by Debris if above size 2.`

# **`[ Footstep Guide ]`**

## `How to set footstep sounds for characters and floor tiles.`

## 

# **`Types & Materials`**

# 

`There are 5 types of feet for characters, and 7 types of materials for Floor tiles. For each combination of foot type and material, there are a set of footstep sounds.`

`To set a Player’s foot type, set their footkind variable.`  
`To set a Floor’s material, set their material variable.`

| `Foot Type` | `Value` | `Example` |  | `Floor Material` | `Value` | `Example` |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `None` | `0` | `YV B-Skin` |  | `None` | `0` | `N/A` |
| `Organic` | `1` | `Fish` |  | `Sand` | `1` | `Desert` |
| `Plant` | `2` | `Plant` |  | `Rock` | `2` | `Scrapyards` |
| `Shoe` | `3` | `Rebel` |  | `Metal` | `3` | `Sewers B-Tiles` |
| `Metal` | `4` | `Robot` |  | `Slimy Sand` | `4` | `Desert B-Tiles` |
|  |  |  |  | `Slimy Rock` | `5` | `Caves B-Tiles` |
|  |  |  |  | `Slimy Metal` | `6` | `N/A` |

`Walking on Carpet (7-3) counts as material 1, and walking on FloorMiddle (HQ3) counts as material 3.`

# 

# **`Timing Footsteps`**

# 

`By default, footstep sounds are hardcoded to play on frame 3 and 6 of a character’s walk sprite. Plant’s steps play on frames 2, 3, and 4, and Robot and Horror’s steps play on frames 1, 3, 4, and 6.`

`If your custom sprite doesn’t match these footstep timings, you could manually time them like so:`

| \#define step 	 // Time Footsteps: 	if(sprite\_index \== spr\_walk && roll \== 0){ 		var \_list \= \[1, 3, 5\]; // Frames 2, 4, and 6 		footstep \= \_list\[0\]; 		with(\_list){ 			if(other.image\_index \< self){ 				other.footstep \= self; 				break; 			} 		} 		footstep \= ((footstep \== 0) ? image\_number : footstep) \- 2; 	} |
| :---- |

`This example would be called from a .race or .skin mod’s step event.`
